findings.finding: The release will carry a post-period AuM figure (last year's was dated 7 Nov) struck after a severe AI/tech sell-off: the Nasdaq 100 was 15.1% below its 6 Oct peak by 20 Nov and the IA Technology sector lost 7.3% in the week to 20 Nov, on a book where Technology was 51% of AuM a year ago and Tech/AI led the inflows since, so the figure will be well below £43.7bn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025 interims carried a rising post-period AuM (£28.4bn at 7 Nov) and the stock still fell 3.65%; the Q2 AuM update on 12 Oct 2026 (AuM -3% q/q despite inflows) moved it -1.6% (805p to 792p).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the market movement can be read from public fund NAVs and indices, and POLR is down 19% from 870p on 30 Sep to 702p (PCT.L -21%, QQQ -12% over the same span), which is about what operating leverage on a 10-15% AuM fall implies. What is left is the headline itself, and possibly a reference date that falls on or after the 20 Nov low.
findings.independence: Trustnet 06 Nov 2026 on the 5 Nov chip crash (technology funds were 15 of the 25 biggest IA fallers, Polar Capital Global Technology among them): https://www.trustnet.com/news/13487983/the-winning-and-losing-funds-when-tech-stocks-crashed-on-5-november

findings.finding: Oct-Nov net flows are at risk of turning: Q2 inflows had already halved from Q1 (£1.2bn vs £2.5bn), were concentrated in Global Technology and AI, and the company itself said it remained 'disciplined in assessing the durability of these flows'; UK active equity funds lost £1.4bn in October (Calastone).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Flow momentum is what re-rated the name in FY26 (FY results +4.26% on 1 Jul 2026 with 'momentum has continued'); a flow reversal has not been printed in the observed history.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody outside the company has the Oct-Nov flow number, so it is genuinely unknown. But the evidence is a proxy: Calastone's October data has no tech breakdown (https://www.trustnet.com/news/13487936/calastone-passive-equity-funds-experience-first-outflows-since-2023), and Liontrust said on 19 Nov that its outflows were slowing. Some of the 19% fall already prices weaker flows.

findings.finding: The first interim dividend under the policy adopted 1 Apr 2026 ('50% of the first half's core profits') will be mechanically far above last year's 14.0p, because H1 average AuM ran at roughly £40bn+ against £23.2bn in H1 FY26, when core operating profit was £25.1m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The interim dividend was held at 14.0p from 2022 to 2025, so a step-up has no reaction history; the 1 Jul 2026 release that introduced the policy rose 4.26%.
findings.why_not_priced: The policy has been public since July and nine analysts model it, so the step-up lands inside what the company guided. My 20-25p figure is my own arithmetic from disclosed AuM, the fee yield and the H1 FY26 cost base, not a sourced estimate. What may not be priced is the retail headline of a dividend up by more than half, on a stock yielding roughly 6.5% on the 46p floor. The board could also temper it under the 'normal circumstances' clause after November, which is why the range goes below zero.
findings.independence: H1 FY26 base (core operating profit £25.1m, average AuM £23.2bn, 75bps yield): https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/polar-capital-holdings--polr/unaudited-interim-results-/9236630; H1 FY27 AuM path: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/polar-capital-holdings--polr/aum-update/9659732

findings.finding: The £15m buyback completed on 6 Aug 2026 and nothing has replaced it, while cash stood at £151m at March and H1 earnings were record. The policy commits surplus capital to buybacks or specials, and the shares now trade about 20% below the programme's final purchases (846p), so a new buyback with the interims is plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The first buyback was announced with the Q3 AuM update on 16 Jan 2026; the price reaction that day was not measured here.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference from capacity and policy. The company has not signalled a new programme, and the EBT bought 103,099 shares at 779.5p on 15 Oct, which is share-award hedging, not a return of capital. If the market expected a buyback, the stock would not have kept making lows into the print.
findings.independence: Capital return policy and cash of £150.99m at 31 Mar 2026: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/polar-capital-holdings--polr/group-audited-results-for-year-ended-31-march-2026/9645640 (the same company, a different document)

lessons_applied: 'You were right about the number and too small about the move' / 'Understatement': abs_move_pct raised from 5.0 to 5.5. The period is pre-released, but profit, the first dividend under the new policy and the post-period AuM are new, and 20d realised vol is 50%; the reaction history (3.65 median) was used as context, not as a cap.

'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series': the flow-reversal finding cut from -0.8 to -0.6, because the evidence is an industry proxy with no tech breakdown and a reporting peer (Liontrust, 19 Nov) said its outflows were slowing.

'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': H1 AuM and inflows kept out of findings (rejected as duplicate). The dividend finding stays small because it lands inside the guided policy.
